Recon Mission

Getting to know the enemy’s weapons and tactics before planning

In a war, the first step toward victory is to expose the enemy’s strategy. This way, we avoid falling into his trap. In Tzivos Hashem we face the trickiest enemy: the Yetzer Hara.

Here’s his strategy: First, the Yetzer Hara plants negative thoughts in our heads. Then, those thoughts grow into worse

feelings that can lead to even more dangerous actions.

One of the ways the Yetzer Hara tricks us is by telling us to be apathetic. This means to be detached and uncaring about what’s happening around us (different from ‘'pathetic’, which means ‘in a pitiful or sorry state). The Yetzer Hara’s goal is for us to shut out other people’s feelings and be insensitive. He tries convincing us that if we think of others, there won’t be any space left to feel our own feelings or properly care for ourselves.

Look at the following scene and identify where the Yetzer Hara could influence you to be apathetic towards others, and trigger your thoughts, speech, and actions.

We have just uncovered another one of the Yetzer Hara’s tricks. He tries getting us to be apathetic and insensitive towards other people and their feelings.

Ask each squad member to think of a time when they fell into the enemy’s trap and behaved apathetically. Identify what thoughts and feelings were created, and how each of you acted.

Don't forget to include Torah, tefillah, tzedakah, and Moshiach in your meeting!

See you next week to learn this battle’s strategy from Rochel Imenu.
